jobs.title: Forensic Analyst - Entry to Mid Level (Maryland)
Forensics - Crisis and Investigations - Cyber Response - Manager

reading.body:
Digital forensics hiring in this sample is government and consulting work, not AI lab work, with three openings posted between September 8 and October 4, 2026.

The pattern is narrow. Two of the three roles are federal: the National Security Agency at Fort Meade, Maryland, and the U.S. Postal Service in Richmond, California. The third is a manager-level cyber response role at EY in McLean, Virginia. Pay spans roughly $87,000 at the entry-to-mid federal level to $192,300 at the top of the consulting band.

This matters for AI only indirectly. Digital forensics is the work of investigating devices and networks after an incident, and it sits downstream of the same data center and network buildout that AI depends on, because more compute and more connected infrastructure mean more surfaces to investigate. The data does not show that link. It shows three employers hiring for it.

What the data does not cover is volume or trend. Three postings drawn from a mix of federal, aggregated, and remote job sources cannot establish whether forensics hiring is rising, falling, or steady, and the salary ranges are posted bands rather than offers. Read it as a snapshot of who is hiring, not as a measure of demand.
